'''Charles F. McMillan''' (October 25, 1954 – September 6, 2024) was an American [[nuclear physicist]] and served as the 10th director of the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]]. His appointment was effective June 1, 2011.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |first=Frank |last=Munger |date=2011-05-26 |title= More than 150 applicants for Los Alamos job; choice of McMillan lauded |newspaper=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]] |url=http://blogs.knoxnews.com/munger/2011/05/more-than-150-applicants-for-l.html |access-date= 27 May 2011 |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20131203014537/http://blogs.knoxnews.com/munger/2011/05/more-than-150-applicants-for-l.html |archive-date=2013-12-03}}</ref> He succeeded [[Michael R. Anastasio]]. On September 5, 2017, McMillan announced he would be leaving his position as director at the end of the year.<ref>{{Cite press release |url=http://www.lanl.gov/discover/news-release-archive/2017/September/0905-mcmillan-to-retire.php |title = Los Alamos Laboratory Director Charles F. McMillan to retire at end of year |date=2017-09-05 |publisher=[[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240319122555/https://www.lanl.gov/discover/news-release-archive/2017/September/0905-mcmillan-to-retire.php |archive-date=2024-03-19 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Charles F. McMillan had been Principal Associate Director for Weapons Programs at Los Alamos and joined the laboratory in 2006, where he was responsible for directing the science, technology, engineering, and infrastructure that enables the Laboratory to deliver on its core mission of ensuring the safety, reliability, and performance of the nation's nuclear deterrent. McMillan was elected by peers to lead the Nuclear Security Enterprise Integration Council.
Established in 1943 as part of the [[Manhattan Project]], Los Alamos National Laboratory is a principal contributor to NNSA's programs to maintain the U.S. nuclear weapons stockpile and to reduce the international dangers posed by weapons of mass destruction.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.energy.gov/national-laboratories |title=National Laboratories |website=[[United States Department of Energy]] |access-date=2026-06-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260603175949/https://www.energy.gov/national-laboratories  |archive-date=2026-06-03 |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Charles McMillan United States Senate testimony.jpg|thumb|right|Charles F. McMillan (left) testifies before the [[United States Senate Committee on Armed Services]], Strategic Forces Subcommittee, May 7, 2013. [[Sandia National Laboratories]] Director [[Paul Hommert]] is to the right.]]

McMillan was also president of [[Los Alamos National Security]], LLC, the company that manages and operates the lab for the [[National Nuclear Security Administration]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Charles McMillan named director of Los Alamos Lab |url=https://link.ucop.edu/2011/05/27/charles-mcmillan-named-director-of-los-alamos-lab/ |date=2011-05-27 |work=Link |publisher=[[University of California|University of California Office of the President]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130202015323/https://link.ucop.edu/2011/05/27/charles-mcmillan-named-director-of-los-alamos-lab/ |archive-date=2013-02-02 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Prior to joining Los Alamos, McMillan, an experimental physicist, spent more than 20 years at [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] in California, beginning in 1983.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.environmental-expert.com/news|title=Environmental Industry News &#124; Environmental XPRT|website=www.environmental-expert.com}}</ref> He held a doctorate in physics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and a [[Bachelor of Science|bachelor of science]] in Mathematics and Physics from [[Washington Adventist University]].<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite news|title=New director named at Los Alamos Lab|author=K. Roark|url=http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/article/25641|newspaper=UC Newsroom|date=26 May 2011|accessdate=3 Oct 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110916112001/http://www.universityofcalifornia.edu/news/article/25641|archive-date=16 September 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>

His annual compensation as director of the laboratory, including benefits and pension value increases, was reported as US$1,081,059 in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://llnlthetruestory.blogspot.com/2012/04/lanl-director-makes-1m.html |title=LANL Director Makes $1M |author=Anonymous |work=LLNL - the True Story |date=2012-04-22}}</ref>

===Personal life and death===
McMillan was awarded two Department of Energy Awards of Excellence. He was married with three children. McMillan was also an avid photographer and accomplished musician, playing piano, organ, and recorder. He continued to perform in a baroque chamber music ensemble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Artist Bios |publisher=The New Mexico Performing Arts Society |url=https://nmpas.org/artists/ |access-date=2024-09-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240916212356/https://nmpas.org/artists/ |archive-date=2024-09-16 |language=en-US}}</ref>

McMillan died in [[Los Alamos, New Mexico]], on September 6, 2024, at the age of 69, as a result of injuries sustained in a traffic collision.<ref>{{Cite news |first1=Carina |last1=Julig |first2=Alaina |last2=Mencinger |date=2024-09-06 |title=Former LANL director Charles McMillan, 69, dies in crash |newspaper=[[The Santa Fe New Mexican]] |url=https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/former-lanl-director-charles-mcmillan-69-dies-in-crash/article_9b8be1a6-6c8e-11ef-bc80-77d8e15a6b11.html}}</ref>

==Events==
Charles F. McMillan presented a lecture on "The Timeline of Technology", offering examples of how innovations in the 20th century are used in this century to solve national and global security, energy and environmental issues, on October 1, 2014, at [[Howard H. Baker, Jr. Center for Public Policy]].<ref>[[Howard H. Baker, Jr. Center for Public Policy]] [http://tntoday.utk.edu/2014/09/26/baker-center-talk-to-feature-los-alamos-national-lab-director/][http://bakercenter.utk.edu/][http://bakercenter.utk.edu/global-security-distinguished-lecture-featuring-charles-mcmillan-wed-oct-1-530-pm-toyota-auditorium/][https://sf.ites.utk.edu/utk/Play/a0f32d187c724aeb8edd2c5c4ea09d671d] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151008174713/https://sf.ites.utk.edu/utk/Play/a0f32d187c724aeb8edd2c5c4ea09d671d|date=2015-10-08}}[https://www.belfercenter.org/event/timeline-technology]</ref> He stressed the importance of Los Alamos to national security, and reflected on the last Divider nuclear test, on September 23, 1992, in [[Operation Julin]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Charles F. |last=McMillan |date=2015-08-06 |title=70 years after Hiroshima, Los Alamos remains essential to our national security |website=[[Fox News]] |url=https://www.foxnews.com/opinion/70-years-after-hiroshima-los-alamos-remains-essential-to-our-national-security |access-date=2026-06-04}}</ref>
